title: Attitudes: Formation, Change & Persuasion
summary: Attitudes: definition, ABC model (affective, behavioural, cognitive), formation and change, cognitive dissonance (Festinger) and persuasion processes.
objectives: Define attitudes and the ABC model.
revision: Attitudes: definition, ABC model, formation, Festinger's cognitive dissonance, persuasion.
traps: Cognitive dissonance = inconsistency discomfort → attitude change (Festinger).

notes.t: A relatively stable evaluation of a person, object or idea, ranging from favourable to unfavourable.

i: Affective component: feelings and emotions toward the attitude object
Behavioural component: actions or intentions toward the object
Cognitive component: beliefs and thoughts about the object
Classical conditioning: pairing object with emotional response
Operant conditioning: reinforcement of attitude-expressing behaviour
Social learning: observing and imitating others
Direct experience: personal contact with the object

notes.t: Leon Festinger's theory: psychological discomfort from holding inconsistent cognitions, motivating attitude change to reduce dissonance.
The Yale model of persuasion identifies source, message, channel and audience as factors that influence attitude change.
UGC NET frequently asks about the ABC model, cognitive dissonance and factors in persuasion.

mnemonics.title: ABCF
mnemonics.text: A — Affective (feelings), B — Behavioural (actions), C — Cognitive (beliefs), F — Festinger cognitive dissonance

flashcards.a: Relatively stable evaluation of person, object or idea.
Discomfort from inconsistent cognitions motivates change.
